deep_analysis: 48h verdict: SHORTs were the right side (+0.15 USDT, 38% WR), LONGs were wrong (-0.86 USDT, 38% WR). We keep firing pump-chain+ LONGs into ranging coins and paying the chop tax. BLUR is the poster child: pump-chain+ fired LONG at 0.009456 expecting a pump, BLUR dumped 1.37% to hard_max_loss (-0.31). The winning side was SHORT - BLUR had been bleeding from 0.00938 to 0.00925 for hours. ARB repeated the same pattern 3x: LONG into a 0.1891-0.1904 range, chop-killed each time. The market is telling us clearly: in this regime, fades of pump signals outperform chasing them. Signal-level confirmation: pump-chain- (SHORT) has 30 trades at 16.7% WR totaling -0.77 - even the shorts from that family lose because they fire in chop too. The winners are volume-buildup- (77.8% WR) and r2v2-long3 (80% WR) - these catch actual trends, not bounces. The RSI 'sweet spot' of 50-60 is actually our worst bucket (n=14, 35.7% WR, avg -0.047) - not because 50-60 is bad, but because we are entering mid-RSI in chop where there is no follow-through. The only profitable RSI bucket is 40-50 (60% WR) - closer to extremes where mean reversion has fuel. Root cause: pump-chain+ detects volume spikes that fizzle in ranging conditions. The signal cannot distinguish 'about to trend' from 'one candle of volume then silence.'
regime_context: BTC is AT EMA300 (81568 vs 81634) with SLOW velocity and NEUTRAL linreg - textbook chop. The 15m and 4h scanners say LONG_BIAS and STRONG_UP trend quality, but the 1m reality is a 81480-81660 range for the past 2 hours with declining volume. This mismatch between higher-TF bias and lower-TF chop is exactly where hard_max_loss trades breed: the signal sees 'bull trend' on 4h, fires LONG, and the 1m chop eats the stop. Portfolio is 1/10 positions - appropriately cautious. The single open BTC LONG sits right at the EMA300 pivot with a tight 0.11% SL; it will resolve quickly but it is a coin flip, not an edge. When BTC is AT EMA300 in chop, the profitable playbook from the last 48h is: wait for a clear break above or below, then ride the trend that follows. Do not position in the middle.

1. PUMP-CHAIN+ LONG FADE PATTERN (n=26, 7d): pump-chain+ has 26.9% WR, avg -0.001, total -0.02. Every pump in chop fizzles. BLUR -0.31, ARB -0.08, ARB -0.10 all from this signal. WINNING side: SHORT the fade - when a coin pumps in chop and stalls, the dump follows. Why weren't we on it? The signal only fires LONG on volume spikes; it has no fade mode.

2. HARD_MAX_LOSS = CHOP ENTRIES (7d, n=20 sampled): 52/56 hard_max_loss trades never reached +0.40% trail arm. Avg duration 28min. The entry conditions were wrong from minute one - there was no trend to catch. WINNING side: not in these trades at all. Capital preserved = profit.

3. RSI 50-60 DEATH ZONE IN CHOP (48h, n=14): WR 35.7%, avg -0.047. Mid-range RSI in chop = no edge. The only green bucket is RSI 40-50 (n=5, 60% WR, avg +0.008). WINNING side: enter closer to extremes where mean reversion has fuel, or skip entirely when RSI is neutral.

4. ARB CHOP MACHINE (48h, 3 losses, total -0.22): Three LONG entries into a 0.1891-0.1904 range. All pump-chain+ or ai-trader+. All hard_max_loss or atr_sl. WINNING side: SHORT the range high or do not trade ARB at all - it has no trend.

5. WINNERS COME FROM TRAILING EXITS (48h): All 10 biggest winners exited via trail_sl, rr_engine_trail_hit, profit-monster-trail, or atr_tp_hit. The system's edge is in catching and riding trends. Losers exit via hard_max_loss, atr_sl_hit, stale_exit - chop entries that never got traction. The fix is not better exits; it is better entries that find trends sooner.
